findings.issue: Deny-to-allow regression in the guards that read runnable_text. _closed_part appends synthetic closers to every part that _context_step reads as ending open. A part can end open because the guards' shell lexer misreads it, not because its shell stops inside a quote. The closers then turn a part the lexer could not tokenize, which HEAD sent to the strict text reading, into a balanced parse, and the destructive line that really runs is read as the inside of a quote. Probed in scratch git-archive exports, HEAD _config.py against the working tree's, by calling guard-history-rewrite decide and guard-uncommitted reading() directly. Shape A, a shell body holding a nested quoted heredoc whose body has an apostrophe: bash <<'EOF' / cat <<'Y' / it's / Y / <VERB> / EOF. The inner shell runs <VERB>. The history guard went from deny to allow for <VERB> = <STASH-DROP> and <FORCE-PUSH>. guard-uncommitted went from (deny, text) to (allow, operation) for <HARD-RESET>. The same happens when the nested heredoc writes a file (cat >f <<'Y'). Shape B, an interpreter body that is valid Python and has an escaped apostrophe: python3 - <<'PY' / print('it\'s') / import os / os.system("<VERB>") / PY. The history guard went from deny to allow for <STASH-DROP> and <FORCE-PUSH>, and guard-uncommitted went from (deny, text) to (allow, operation) for <HARD-RESET>. Variants with an even number of apostrophes were already allowed at HEAD, so this class existed before. The diff extends it to the odd case, which used to fail closed. The docstring's safety argument at 3463 ('what a closer seals is text its own shell never runs') does not hold in these shapes. The sealed text is a heredoc body or Python source that does run. The diff also re-points gu51 off its heredoc fixture because 'the fix now parses' it, so no case pins that a bodied command the lexer cannot read reaches the text reading.
findings.resolution: Stop sealing a part with closers it does not have. Grade each part on its own parse, as the task asked: runnable_text returns the parts, or the callers (git_invocations, command_clauses and the secrets guard's views) iterate them. If any part does not tokenize alone, send the command to the strict text reading over the whole view, as HEAD did. Correct the docstring at 3463. Add deny cases for shapes A and B with each verb, in test_guard_history_rewrite.py and guard-uncommitted's selftest. Restore a gu51-style case that pins a bodied, untokenizable command to the text reading. Prove each new case red against the current _closed_part.

preExisting.issue: _shell_text and _executed_text still join the command text and the heredoc bodies raw, so quote state crosses between parts in the way runnable_text did. The executor reported this and left it (outside the task's files). No allow was measured for it.
preExisting.resolution: File it as a fault. Fix it with the same per-part reading that finding 1 asks for, not with closers.

preExisting.issue: A nested heredoc inside a shell-fed body is not split out. The lexer reads that inner body as shell, so a body with an even number of apostrophes hides the next line. It was allowed at HEAD as well: bash <<'EOF' / cat <<'Y' / it's / Y / <VERB> / echo ' / EOF.
preExisting.resolution: Run split_heredocs on each shell body, recursively, before grading it. Add a case that pins the even-count variant.

intent.note: Clause: 'grade each shell-fed body on its own rather than concatenated after the text, so no quote state crosses from the text into a body'. Diff: `return "\n".join(_closed_part(p) for p in [text] + shell + code)` (_config.py:3472). The parts are still concatenated into one view that is graded once. Each part is first sealed with synthetic closers and a pending-escape space. The purpose half is met for the measured shapes: no quote crosses into a later part (qv1's eight shapes; gk34-gk41; gu54). The mechanism half diverges. A body is not graded on its own parse: a closed rewrite of it is graded, and that rewrite produces finding 1's deny-to-allow regression. Clause: 'red-first the measured shape and its no-apostrophe twin'. The measured shape is red at HEAD (gk34, gk38, gu54, qv1). The twin (gk35, gk39, s80) is green at HEAD, because the description itself says it was already denied, so it can only be a lock. Claim versus diff: the technical outcome describes the mechanism accurately (closing via _context_step, comment skip, no-body passthrough, gu51 re-pointed, gu54 added). It omits a behaviour change: a bodied command whose part the lexer cannot tokenize no longer reaches the strict reading. The executor's own gu51 note ('which the fix now parses as an operation') is that change, and the claim treats it as harmless. The dependants answer for guard-release is accurate. It also detects more publishers now: the publishing probe went from false to true on tag shapes behind a body.
